issueObservations.rationale: FR2314156865 still shows FedRAMP Certified, Rev5 Agency Class D. The public package object has an empty certified_services list. The February matrix and October/November limited vendor announcements retain their separate dates and qualifications.
F1607197917 still shows FedRAMP Certified, Rev5 Agency Class C. Its embedded public certified_services array is empty. Named product and component coverage remains distinct from the offering status.

The current AWS Victoria row and relevant 10.7 change-log entry show Israel. Both public Cloud comparison exports retain the current evidence with historical qualifications. Indexed AWS lists il-central-1, which supplies endpoint evidence only.

Both old and 10.8 ACS tables label High Victoria No and Classic Yes. Adjacent compliance prose says both. The operation-specific maintenance window guide excludes High, and the reader keeps the operation-specific qualification.

10.7 and 10.8 Service Details name Moderate for AWS S3 federation, excluding High and IL5, while the April 8 change-log row specifically describes High/IL5 availability for relevant 10.3. Preserve both account scopes and the distinct restrictions for other federation variants.
The Observability service table maps us2 to Google Cloud Oregon, while the US Database Monitoring row lists us2 and None under Google Cloud. The public report retains this contradiction.

All 22 About and 21 Cloud installer regional rows in SAIA 2.3.6 were compared, matching everywhere except the June 28, 2024 Dublin overview listing omitted by the installer. The public Dublin reports, offline HTML and real PDFs retain that difference and feature-specific Agent Mode scope.

The About section lists SAIA 2.2.0+, ITSI 5.0.0+ and MCP Server 1.2.1+ plus six tools. Dublin has no separate ITSI subagent rollout statement. Both public Dublin ITSI reports retain that qualification.

The Agent Mode requirements use supported AWS regions and enabled Model Runtime. Its separate runtime table describes Dublin Global from 2.3.0, with no zone/country guarantee. The Cloud Connected installation assurance does not answer that feature-specific routing question.

2.2.0–2.3.6 installation exclusion and the 2.1.1 fallback without Agent Mode remain documented. The new 2.4.0 installer establishes a fresh qualified Cloud Connect path and preserves separate supported-region, permission and Model Runtime prerequisites.

The October feature announcement names SPL authoring/explanation in High. The current 2.4.0 notes describe the same core functions in supported High environments and explicitly exclude Agent Mode. The 2.3.6 IL2 hosted-model restriction is a separately versioned statement.

The full ES 8.8 Essentials/Premier/Cloud Connect tables maintain the Montréal and Calgary distinctions, GovCloud exceptions and separate GCP/Azure statements. Both public CMP views accurately display the named Montréal exception.

The currently published Assistant Availability list names us3. The current service realm equivalence table lacks that row. A mapped Virginia realm and the Troubleshooting Agent operation prerequisites provide no new mapping.
The renamed 8.8 aggregate shows Cloud ES 8.6+ and the linked task gives 8.7+. Current CMP installation prerequisites and dated 8.7 scope stay separate.
The current 8.8 availability column says Premier Cloud only while compatibility also contains CMP. The separate task explicitly remains Controlled Availability and does not establish CMP rollout.
The renamed 8.8 parent gives 200 analyses and 20 revisions in the defined scopes. Its linked task retains first ten, findings per day and no rerun. The semantic difference remains unresolved.

The two retired 8.8 locators returned HTTP 404. The current Agentic offerings and Setting up the Triage and Response topics are the substantively reviewed replacements. Retain the access history and independent premise conflicts.
The scoped 8.8 Response task retains no reruns, no later-added findings after processing and frontier models only. The Triage parent revision description is a different component.
